Hypoglycemia is highly plausible—neonates are metabolically vulnerable, and hypoglycemia frequently presents with lethargy and seizures, often within the first 24–48 hours; it is rapidly reversible and must be ruled out immediately with point-of-care glucose. Intracranial hemorrhage (especially in preterm infants or after traumatic delivery) can cause acute neurological deterioration and seizures; imaging (cranial ultrasound or MRI) is key. Pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy is rarer but must be considered in early-onset intractable seizures—though usually presents earlier (first days), it can manifest with lethargy and seizures responsive only to pyridoxine; empiric trial is low-risk and diagnostically clarifying.
